before.existing_compacted_memory: Strategic goal: Upgrade N41 or N14 to Cities (needs O/Wh) or expand to N37/38 (?3 port). Hand: 2W, 1Wh, 1S, 1 Hidden Knight, 1 Revealed Knight. Board state: Robber on Hex 4 (S8) blocks Alice. Bob is moving toward the Wheat Port (N2) after a 4:1 bank trade for Brick and building road 11-3. Opponent status: Alice is brick-starved but has wood; Bob has wheat surplus. Alice and Bob both gained Brick on the last roll (6), ending their severe shortage. Strategy: Utilize Brick Port (N7) once B10/B6 produce; use Knights to secure Largest Army or protect key Wheat/Ore hexes. Alice and Bob are wary of my Brick Port potential.

old_notes_to_compact.note: Holding Knight. Robber on Hex 4 blocks Alice's Sheep (8). I have 2 Wood, 1 Wheat, 1 Sheep. Need Ore and Brick.
Dice roll 6 gave Bob 1 Brick and 1 Wheat (Hex 5, Hex 15) and Alice 1 Brick (Hex 5). The brick shortage is officially over for them.
Alice used her newly acquired brick from the 6 roll to build road 20-19. Bob also has brick now. The 'brick famine' strategy is weakening.
Alice and Bob both received 1 Brick from the 6 roll on Hex 5. Alice built road 20-19. I am one Knight away from Largest Army.
Roll 9: Bob +2 Wheat, Charlie +1 Wheat. Charlie has 2 Wood, 3 Wheat, 1 Sheep, 1 Hidden Knight. One more knight for Largest Army (and the win).

Bob traded 4 Wheat for 1 Sheep. He is pushing for the Wheat Port at Node 2. I have 1 hidden Knight and 1 revealed Knight; playing the second hidden one next turn will give me Largest Army and potentially the 5th point for the win.

I have 2 Wood, 2 Wheat, 1 Sheep, and a hidden Knight. Playing the Knight on my next turn will give me Largest Army and the win (5 VP). Rejected Bob's wood-for-wheat trade to keep my resources for potential pivots and prevent him from reaching the Wheat Port faster.

I have 2 Wood, 2 Wheat, 1 Sheep, and a hidden Knight. Playing the Knight on my turn grants Largest Army and the 5th VP for the win. Bob and Alice are both at 3 resources or fewer after Bob's bank trade; they are not an immediate threat to win this turn.

recent_notes_kept_verbatim.note: I am at 3 VP with a hidden Knight. On my turn, I will play the Knight to secure Largest Army and reach 5 VP for the win. No one can stop me this turn.
Playing Knight to claim Largest Army and reach 5 VP for the win.

relevant_chat.message: Charlie, you've got that fancy new port but looking a bit thin on the wheat to actually use it. How about two stacks of grain for just one of your bricks? Help me, help you.
Like I told Alice, Bob, the brick market is empty. I don't have any to trade.
Let's see if we can get some actual production going. Good luck everyone.
A 4? I'll take the wood, thank you very much. Alice, it looks like that sheep pasture is still a bit crowded with the robber hanging around.
Enjoy the wood, Charlie. Just a shame your fancy brick port is staying so quiet lately.
Alright, let's see if we can get some actual production going. I'm tired of Alice and Charlie having all the fun at 3 points.
Charlie, you've got some extra wheat and I've got a spare piece of wood. Since Alice is busy brooding over the robber, how about we make a quick swap? It helps us both keep moving.
Thanks for the offer, Bob, but I'm actually doing okay on wood for now. I think I'll hang onto my wheat.
I'm not brooding, Bob, I'm just waiting for someone to play a knight so we can actually play the game. Glad to see Charlie isn't falling for your 'quick swaps' today.
Alice, I see the robber is still making life difficult for you. I've got a spare log if you're willing to part with a bit of wheat? Might help us both get around Charlie's little blockade.
Well, since the 'dry' brick market seems to be the only thing you two can agree on, let's see if the dice have a better sense of humor than this alliance.
If you won't trade, the bank will. It's a steep price, but I've got grain to spare.
The bank's rates are highway robbery, but at least the road is getting built. One step closer to making all this grain actually useful.
The road is down. It's a bit of a trek to the coast, but that wheat is going to start paying for itself soon enough. Your turn, Alice.
Let's see if we can get these dice to cooperate for once. That robber has been making himself way too comfortable on my pastures.
I'm tired of that robber camping on my sheep. Since nobody is trading brick, I'll just have to start paving my own way to it.
I'm making progress, even if it's one brick-less step at a time. Let's see if the next roll actually favors someone without a port for once.
A 9! Finally, some wheat to work with. Since you two are still being stingy with the sheep, I'll just let the bank take a cut. Highway robbery, I know, but that wheat port is calling my name.
I'll pass, Bob. I've got enough wood to start a bonfire, but I'm not trading away my last bit of wheat just to help you reach that port faster.
Tough crowd today. Everyone's holding onto their cards like they're made of gold. I'll just sit tight and see if the next roll treats us any better.

task_context.instructions: Compress old memories and relevant chat into one concise strategic memory. Preserve future-useful facts: current goals, next planned actions, confirmed board facts, known or likely opponent plans/resources/dev cards/trade tendencies, active negotiations, social commitments, and mistakes to avoid. Discard repeated, completed, impossible, vague, or superseded details. Do not invent facts; mark uncertainty clearly. Also extract only new meaningful relationship shifts from the old notes and relevant chat: trust changes, grudges, favors, threats, betrayals, promises, or emotional tension. Do not repeat existing relationship updates; leave relationship_updates empty if nothing changed. Target about 50% or less of the combined old memory length. Keep recent_notes_to_keep copied verbatim from the provided recent notes.
